chunks: Regarding a man who bequeathed with a bequest, and his inheritors were witnesses [to it] and they endorsed it. But when the man died, they invalidated the bequest. Is it for them to repudiate what they had agreed with [beforehand]? He said: That is not for them. The bequest is binding upon them if they had accepted it during his (deceased's) lifetime.
Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — similar [narration].

key_terms.أَجَازَ: To endorse/approve — here, the heirs' formal consent to the terms of the will
key_terms.أَقَرَّ: To acknowledge/affirm — formal legal acknowledgment that creates binding obligation
key_terms.جَائِزَة: Binding/valid/enforceable — the ruling that the bequest is legally effective against them
key_terms.وَصِيَّة: Bequest/will — the testamentary disposition made before death

ai.seo_question: If heirs endorse a bequest during the testator's lifetime, can they revoke it after death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that if heirs witness and endorse a bequest during the testator's lifetime, they cannot later invalidate it after his death. This hadith addresses a critical question in Islamic inheritance law: the binding nature of a prior acknowledgment. In Shia jurisprudence, the heirs' prior consent during the testator's lifetime creates an irrevocable legal obligation, preventing them from exploiting their position as inheritors to overturn what they had already agreed to.
